transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Orion Edge), Jamie Lopez (Orion Edge), Rina Tanaka (Orion Edge)

Summary:
A focused partner co-sell workshop to align on joint accounts, refine the go-to-market pitch, validate security/compliance concerns (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and agree next steps for a pilot co-sell program. High-level asks: a joint exec briefing, benchmark data from Redwood for typical latency and costs (hosted vs dedicated), and a clear list of target accounts from Orion.

Topics:
- Partner GTM messaging and one-pager
- Account prioritization and joint outreach cadence
- Technical gating: VPC/private deployment, SOC2 artifacts, KMS/SAML integration
- Pricing and co-sell margin conversation (reseller vs referral)
- Pilot scope and timeline

Action items (captured above): see action_items metadata

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh Samir, Jamie, Rina, great to see you. We'll run about 50, ish minutes, try to leave time for next steps. Liam and I from Redwood — I'll kick off with the GTM objectives and then Liam will cover the technical play.

[00:26] Samir Patel: Hey Maya, thanks. Super excited. We wanted to make this fairly tactical — like, which accounts we should push together and what the ask is from each side.

[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally. So high level, Redwood's goal is to identify 8 to 10 priority accounts where Orion has a strong channel presence, we can bring a pre-sales pitch and a bench to show latency/cost savings. We'll align on spokespeople and a cadence.

[01:05] Jamie Lopez: Quick callout — our sales org is split EMEA/NA, and we have two folks focused on fintech. We would like to pilot in fintech and retail, if that helps narrow things.

[01:28] Liam O'Connor: That's helpful — fintech often cares about latency and data residency. From an infra perspective, Redwood supports hosted API and Dedicated pools; we also have Private/VPC options for regulated workloads. For pilots we usually recommend starting hosted for speed, then migrate to dedicated or private as the account needs isolation.

[01:55] Rina Tanaka: When you say hosted, is data retained anywhere? We have customers who require no logs and customer-managed keys.

[02:10] Liam O'Connor: Good question. Hosted can be configured with short retention, but for strict requirements you hit Private — VPC-onprem or customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) integration. There are separate contracts for that.

[02:33] Samir Patel: Our procurement team will want SOC2 evidence and SSO/SAML integration details before we go to co-sell. Do you have a standard security playbook?

[02:50] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share the security playbook and SOC2 package. Liam can point to typical artifacts and redlines we've seen.

[03:04] Liam O'Connor: Right — we can share SOC2 summary, our architecture diagram, and a checklist for the VPC/on-prem footprint. Note: some customers try to use 'dedicate' nodes — sorry, dedicated — and we see a latency bump during tails if batching is misconfigured, so we usually recommend particular batching profiles.

[03:30] Jamie Lopez: Sounds good. On the GTM side, what co-sell models have you done with other partners? Referral? Revenue share?

[03:45] Maya Chen: We do a few things: referral with a success fee, co-sell with joint discounting (we model margins), and in some cases a reseller arrangement for committed capacity. We can walk through sample economics.

[04:05] Samir Patel: For Orion, we prefer a referral + joint-op with a small kickback for active deals. Reseller is tougher for regulatory reasons.

[04:20] Liam O'Connor: From a technical sell POV, we should also scope a short pilot (2–4 weeks) with a test account: sample prompts, expected qps, latency SLOs. That helps economics and the pitch.

[04:40] Maya Chen: Okay let's map responsibilities. We'll propose a 3-week pilot: week 0 setup, week 1 pilot run, week 2 bench and triage, week 3 exec review.

[05:02] Rina Tanaka: Who does the infra work during week 0? Our side or Redwood?

[05:12] Liam O'Connor: Depends: for hosted we mostly do config and provide keys; for Private/VPC we'll need network handoffs from Orion. For the pilot I'd recommend hosted with a secure enclave and a temp SOP for logging. That minimizes infra lift.

[05:34] Samir Patel: Got it. Let's talk accounts — we have an upper-mid fintech client, "VanguardPay" — they are focused on KYC flows and data residency, hosted might be okay if we can do short retention, but they might want private eventually.

[05:56] Maya Chen: VanguardPay is a great fit. We can show a demo of Redwood's prompt caching for repeated KYC flows which reduces per-token cost. Liam, can you pull typical numbers for a 3-call KYC flow?

[06:15] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, rough rule of thumb — with prefix caching and a smaller model variant, you can cut tokens by ~40% for repeated flows and latency stays in the 90–140ms per-token range depending on hardware. I'll give a spreadsheet with hosted vs dedicated econ.

[06:38] Jamie Lopez: How does quantization impact quality? DeepServe's sales deck said aggressive quantization reduces hallucinations.

[06:51] Liam O'Connor: Heh, that's an interesting claim. Quantization reduces model size and cost, but it can change logits slightly — sometimes a small quality hit. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload; we run eval prompt-sets to ensure quality parity. We'll include eval results for typical KYC prompts.

[07:15] Samir Patel: Any red flags on SOC2 or data residency for VanguardPay?

[07:22] Maya Chen: Nothing immediate. We'll need the customer's compliance checklist. Rina, can Orion share VanguardPay's compliance docs or gating checklist?

[07:33] Rina Tanaka: I can try. I might not have the full checklist but I'll get the primary points.

[07:45] Maya Chen: Great. Next, outreach motion — Samir, what's your suggested cadence for joint BD?

[07:52] Samir Patel: We do a two-week program: initial intro email, follow with joint demo, then exec intro after warm interest. For co-sell, we'd prefer to have a one-pager and a joint ROI slide to hand to AE.

[08:08] Maya Chen: We'll send a co-sell one-pager and a joint ROI template. Jamie, any preferred messaging hooks?

[08:18] Jamie Lopez: Focus on cost predictability and data governance. Also highlight the ability to fall back to smaller models or cached responses during spikes — that's a practical ask from customers.

[08:35] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Redwood has routing policies — we can configure fallback to cheaper model variants automatically. We also support tracing and token-level cost breakdowns in the console for post-mortem.

[08:51] Samir Patel: How easy is it to show those metrics to a customer in a call?

[08:58] Liam O'Connor: We can export dashboards or provide read-only console snapshots; for pilot we usually prep a deck with key charts.

[09:15] Maya Chen: Okay, on procurement timeline, what are typical procurement blockers, Jamie?

[09:23] Jamie Lopez: Enterprise legal will ask about data egress, indemnity, and an SLA. We need to know what SLA Redwood offers for dedicated and hosted.

[09:35] Liam O'Connor: Our Dedicated customers have SLA-backed latency/uptime targets in contracts. Hosted APIs have a different SLA tier. I'll include a short doc comparing SLA tiers. NOTE: SLA terms vary by commitment level.

[09:56] Rina Tanaka: For the pilot should we use an NDA? We prefer a simple mutual NDA before exchanging SOC2 artifacts.

[10:05] Maya Chen: Yes that makes sense. We'll propose a mutual NDA and a data protection addendum if needed.

[10:18] Samir Patel: Competitors — we've had AICorp try to sell us a bundled model offering, CloudServe is also in our pipeline but lacks the quantization tooling. Any differentiation we should call out?

[10:31] Maya Chen: Focus on production economics and observability: token-level cost, KV caching, and model routing. Also speak to our hybrid deployment options — many vendors don't offer a first-class private/VPC orchestration like we do.

[10:48] Jamie Lopez: Good call. On pricing, what's the typical discount structure for co-sell?

[10:55] Maya Chen: We can do referral fees for introductions, or an agreed customer discount and a margin share for active deals. We'll model a sample with placeholder numbers.

[11:10] Liam O'Connor: Back on the technical side — if VanguardPay requires customer-managed KMS, that adds a 2–3 week onboarding overhead typically.

[11:24] Rina Tanaka: That's okay as long as procurement knows.

[11:30] Samir Patel: Let's identify two additional accounts — "Mercato Retail" (retail, conversational commerce) and "PulseHealth" (healthcare, PII concerns). PulseHealth may push for Private deployment.

[11:50] Maya Chen: Ok, so three pilots: VanguardPay (fintech), Mercato (retail), PulseHealth (healthcare). We'll prioritize Vanguard and PulseHealth for compliance conversations.

[12:05] Jamie Lopez: For PulseHealth we need HIPAA assurance. Do you handle BAA?

[12:13] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Redwood can sign a BAA in Private deployments; hosted requires eval. We'll flag that in the security playbook.

[12:25] Maya Chen: Great. Now let's walk through a sample co-sell email/template. I'll read an abridged version.

[12:35] Maya Chen: "Hi <Account> — Orion Edge and Redwood have partnered to bring secure, cost-effective LLM inference for regulated workloads..." (reads)

[12:55] Jamie Lopez: Maybe lead with a customer story — quick stat on cost reduction.

[13:04] Maya Chen: Good, we'll bake that in. Liam, can you give a quick walkthrough of the benchmarking spreadsheet you mentioned?

[13:12] Liam O'Connor: Sure — columns: request pattern, tokens per request, model variant, batching policy, estimated cost per 1k requests, latencies (p50/p90), recommended deployment. For example, conversational retail at 20 qps with caching can use a smaller model variant and hit p50 of ~80ms.

[13:40] Samir Patel: Are these numbers AWS/GPU specific? We want region-aware numbers because our accounts are EU heavy.

[13:50] Liam O'Connor: I'll include region modifiers. We also include hardware mappings (A100 vs H100 vs Ampere) in the sheet, though we tend to normalize to cost per token to keep it portable.

[14:04] Rina Tanaka: The sheet should also show the fallback costs if you route to a cheaper model during spikes — that's important for finance to see.

[14:14] Liam O'Connor: Yes good point, I'll add a fallback scenario.

[14:24] Maya Chen: Ok switching gears — who owns outreach? Samir, does Orion want to own initial intro and Redwood join for the demo?

[14:33] Samir Patel: Yes ideally Orion opens, we do a quick intro email, then Redwood does the demo. For strategic accounts we want executive-to-exec after the demo.

[14:45] Jamie Lopez: Also can we do a co-branded one-pager for sales enablement? A single PDF that AE's can send.

[14:53] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll co-brand and share a lightweight enablement kit.

[15:02] Rina Tanaka: About legal — we will need a sample contract and SOW for pilot. Can Redwood share a template?

[15:10] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share a pilot SOW and a sample MSA. Note: any private deployment SOW will include network and on-prem requirements.

[15:24] Samir Patel: On tracking leads, do you have a preferred CRM handoff? HubSpot? Salesforce?

[15:31] Maya Chen: Salesforce is our primary. We can set up a shared campaign and a joint pipeline view. We'll need account IDs and champion emails.

[15:44] Jamie Lopez: We can export ABs soon.

[15:50] Liam O'Connor: Small technical caveat: for any pilot that intends to test throughput, we need a test harness or simulated traffic; production traffic will surface different perf characteristics. We can help build a harness.

[16:10] Maya Chen: Great. Let's capture pilot success criteria — what must be true to call the pilot a win?

[16:20] Samir Patel: 1) Latency meets the agreed p90 SLO, 2) Cost per request within 10% of projected model, 3) No major security gating issues (SOC2/BAA resolved), 4) A sales-ready case study or exec review.

[16:40] Jamie Lopez: Add: customer signs letter of intent or next-step commitment to move to a paid pilot within 60 days.

[16:50] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll put those in the SOW.

[17:05] Rina Tanaka: One more compliance question: do you provide audit logs and access controls for multi-team access? We need RBAC and audit trails.

[17:14] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Redwood Console supports role-based access, audit logging, and can integrate with SAML SSO for enterprise. For Private we can push logs into your SIEM as well.

[17:30] Samir Patel: If we run into data residency constraints, what's the fastest path?

[17:36] Liam O'Connor: Typically spin up a regionally located dedicated pool / private node. That can be done in 2–6 weeks depending on capacity.

[17:50] Maya Chen: Okay shifting back to GTM — let's pick a launch timeline. Samir, how soon can Orion commit to running outreach?

[17:58] Samir Patel: We can start outreach the week of April 20th if we have assets and the pilot SOW by April 12th.

[18:10] Maya Chen: That aligns with our timeline. We'll aim to have one-pager and SOW draft by Apr 9–12.

[18:22] Jamie Lopez: For the executive briefing, would April 20–24 work for us?

[18:29] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll tentatively schedule and confirm after we share availabilities.

[18:40] Liam O'Connor: Quick note about integrations: if Orion wants to embed Redwood calls into Orion's managed service, we should discuss token provisioning and API keys lifecycle — we have patterns for rotating keys and tenant isolation.

[18:58] Rina Tanaka: Good to know — we'll surface that to our integrations team.

[19:06] Samir Patel: Anything else on the technical front?

[19:10] Liam O'Connor: One last piece — we recommend doing an initial small-batch run at normal traffic levels and then a stress test to observe autoscaling and tails. We'll include a runbook.

[19:28] Maya Chen: Great. Quick competitor note — if CloudServe tries to undercut, call out our predictable pricing and tooling for cost monitoring.

[19:42] Jamie Lopez: One small request: can Redwood share a 1-page comparo vs two major competitors? That helps internal comms.

[19:50] Maya Chen: Yes we'll prepare a neutral comparo slide.

[20:02] Samir Patel: Ok let's wrap with explicit next steps — who owns what.

[20:10] Maya Chen: I'll send: co-sell one-pager, enablement kit, pilot SOW template, and the security playbook (NDA first).

[20:22] Liam O'Connor: I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and a short doc on SLA tiers and region-specific notes.

[20:30] Rina Tanaka: I'll gather the compliance checklist and point you to our SOC2 contact.

[20:36] Samir Patel: I'll share the prioritized account list and champion contacts.

[20:42] Jamie Lopez: I'll confirm exec availability for the week of April 20th.

[20:48] Maya Chen: Perfect. Anything else before we close?

[20:54] Samir Patel: No, thanks all. This was super helpful.

[21:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and proposed calendar invites.

[21:10] End of recording (discussion continues off-record on scheduling)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-attribution and filler words. Some proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., model names), we preserved natural speech patterns and brief overlapping comments.
